off_c.off_10: Hey, boss. I'm back.
I read about FlexiSearch in TechChomp. Good job.
Yeah, about that...
Something wrong?
The company went through a hostile takeover. I was fired.
Oh, so that's why you're here. Well, you're free to help around. But who was the buyer?
A business partner. Called himself Steelman.
You mean RJS?
You know him!?
Yeah, big name in the open source community. He built Leinux with that Leignis guy. Speaking of which, I think he came here looking for you.
For me? What does he want with me?
He wouldn't tell me, only that he said it was important. I can track him down if you want. But that will take a while. And in the meantime those shelves won't organize themselves.
I found Leignis.
I'm only here because you promised me a sauna.
Sorry, I lied. There's no Leignis here.
Are you the one who warned me about RJS?
What's it to you?
You knew that he was dangerous, didn't you?
I wouldn't say he's dangerous. Just misguided.
What do you mean by that?
Do you know about Leinix?
Yes.
We built it together. I had an operating system and RJS had programs to run on it. We partnered together. Without him it would be another failed Unix operating system.
But something happened?
Yes, we had a disagreement. RJS wanted Leinux to be free. Completely free.
And that is a bad thing?
I used to agree with him. But unfortunately this is the real world, we have to make sacrifices for our freedom. RJS doesn't understand that.
I read about it in the news, you two broke up.
I wouldn't say that, we're still friends. But we don't see eye to eye with each other ever since the Tivoization incident.
I think I heard about that. Wasn't that a DRM thing?

It's not just about DRM. It's about the freedom to use the software how you want. RJS didn't see it that way. He said that in order to preserve your freedoms he must take away the freedoms of others. That's a bridge too far for me.
RJS did a hostile takeover on my company.
Sorry about that. RJS has been acquiring companies using a combination of venture capital and open source licenses. I did not want you to get involved in that.
I'm going to take him down.
What?
What!?
He has way more resources than you. There is no way you can take him down.
I took down Relentless. And they said that was impossible.
OK, but if you're actually serious about this you should at least know what you're dealing with.

story_records.off_8: Small Poll For My New Operating System

off_c.off_10: Nice kernel you have here.
It's not as good as yours.
Well, actually. We've been having some problems with our kernel. I'm thinking of teaming up.
Sure, we're already using a lot of your software which means we're using your license.
Great.
That was the first time I met Steelman.
So how did you break up?
I'm getting to that part.
Steelman, I don't think I will be adopting SPL 3.
Why not?
There's just so many restrictions in it like DRM and patents. It's just too complicated.
Those restrictions are there to protect user freedoms. You said so yourself, Leinix is about freedom.
But what if the contributors are scared away by your license? Sometimes we have to limit freedoms for progress.
So there's nothing I can do to change your mind?
I'll think about it. But in the meantime we're sticking with SPL 2.
I think I have a solution to our licensing problem. It's a new draft of the SPL, it's a lesser version.
Yeah, Steelman, I've been talking with the other contributors and they think you should step down from the Leinix Foundation.
Step down? But I built this operating system!
You build user space. And you did a good job, but this is kernel space and the other contributors feel like you're changing the rules on them unnecessarily.
But I'm doing it to prevent companies from taking advantage of us. Didn't you say that Leinix was about freedom?

This isn't about freedom, this is about control. You're power hungry. As long as developers give back their changes I'm happy. I don't care about DRM or patents or tivoization. All I care about is the code.
And what about the users? What about them?
That's not my concern.
So you don't care about your users?
They are free to make their own decisions. We make software, we do not enforce rules.
I can't believe this. You sold out. I knew it was a mistake to trust all these corporations.
I’m not selling out. I’m making Leinix better. More companies using it means more code, more improvements.
Improvements? Like locking users out with DRM and patents? You're letting the corporations control Leinix. You say I'm power hungry? I think you're the one that's high on power.
Enough, I am not going to let you wage your ideological war while the people that wrote the code suffer.
You should go before either of us does something we regret.
Fine. But Leignis, this isn't over yet. You may have given up on the users, but I haven't. I will build my age of free software, just don't get in my way.
That was the last time I heard from him.
What happened after?

I continued to develop Leinix, waiting for the year of Leinix on the desktop. And Steelman went back to the Liberal Software Conservancy. Don't know what happened to him, but I've heard rumours about something called 'The Great Reset'.
I'm going to stop him.
You can't do it by yourself. And we don't even know what The Great Reset even is.
He took everything from me. I took down Relentless, I can take him down too. This so-called Great Reset is just more of a reason to do it.
OK, but I still have no idea how we could do it.
We can start with Relentless, their CEO knows Steelman. We need to find out what he knows.
And how are you going to do that?
I'll get a job at Relentless and work my way up from there.
I got access to Taffy's emails.
Anything about the great reset?
Not yet.
Keep looking.
I found something.
What is it?
The great reset is a license update.
The Standard Public License 4?
You've heard of it?
No, but it's about time they updated it. What's new in version 4?
Sounds like a bunch of patent and trademark stuff.
I think I recall version 3 having stuff like that but it didn't get through. So he's going to force it through now?
Looks that way, I'll talk to him.
Who?
Taffy. I have to learn more about the license.
Are you sure?
Yes, I have to do it.
What is this Great Reset I keep hearing about?
It's nothing that you have to worry about.
But it keeps on coming up.
It's just a license change.
What's in the new license?
Just patent and trademark stuff. Things we were trying to get into SPL 3.
You were trying to do it in the SPL 3?
Yeah, but there was a lot of community pushback. I think we have enough goodwill this time that we can force it through.
Aren't you worried about negative consequences of the license?
What do you mean?
Well, if you remove patent and trademark protections it could cause a lot of IP theft.
So it's unfair, you're stealing from other companies.
That's none of my concern.
But in the long end it would disincentivize innovation.
I don't think I'm the right person to talk to about this.
That's the service they stole.
What?
SuperSearch. They built it on stolen technology.
There's nothing we can do about that now.
I guess you're right.
I found it. Here's the full text of the SPL 4.
What's in it?
Here's the part on patents, 'No entity may enforce trademark or patent claims on software distributed under SPL 4, regardless of prior agreements or legal rights'.

They also increased their copyleft efforts. Now if you're interacting with the software through an API you also get access to the source code and you also have to be using an SPL 4 compatible license.
This is going to kill the software industry.
It won't kill it, it'll consolidate it under the Liberal Software Conservancy and their network of companies.
How are we going to stop it?
It's impossible. We have no case. The only way we could possibly compete is if we make our own OS that beats out Leinix, correcting my mistake all those years ago.
Then we do that.
You want to write your own competing OS that somehow beats out Leinix? Are you crazy?
You said it yourself, it's the only way. And it's not that hard, all we have to do is make a POSIX compatible OS kernel free from the SPL.
I don't like our odds, but I guess it is possible.
I've had it with all these segfaults. How do I get rid of them?
You get good.
There has to be a better way.
Well there is this new language that you could use called Rust. It's supposed to be memory safe meaning no segfaults.
We'll use it.
Just to avoid some segfaults? Programmers these days.
I've been thinking
Yeah?
We should do a microkernel.
That thing Tanenbaum was talking about? I thought you said it was a bad idea.
It was a bad idea in the 1990s, but kernel design has come a long way since the days of the Mach kernel. Now we have an L4 microkernel architecture.
And what does that do?
It's 20 times faster than Mach. Still a bit slower than a monolith and we will have to write a POSIX shim but there are significant benefits to security.
Then let's do it.
It compiles! And it hasn't crashed yet.
That's a good start. We should put it on GitForge and get some traction.
What should we call it though?
How about Leinix 2?
First of all there's already a Leinix 2. And second of all we don't have the trademark.
I do have the trademark actually. But I see your point. What should we call it?
Well, if this is the next kernel after Leinix, why not Nexix?
I'm not a fan. But I wasn't a fan of Leinix either when I first heard of it. I wanted to call it Freax. Hey, why don't we use Freax?
We're going with Nexix.
Fine.
OK, I think that should be enough. I'll post it on Gitforge.
Now we need to promote it.
How do we do that?
Announcements, blog posts, tutorials, and benchmarks. People love benchmarks.
OK, I'll do that.
But you have to keep making a continuous stream of new updates. Otherwise we won't have anything to write about.
If your updates get ahead of you, you can make a release.
We have a problem.
What is it?
The LSC just announced SPL 4
When is it being enforced?
Next summer.
Damn. That doesn't give us a lot of time to prepare.
The OS is ready though.
Well, that depends on your definition of ready.
